requirements.text: Students should be able to manage their loans online, including borrowing, renewing, checking availability, and viewing outstanding fines.
Students should be able to book study rooms online with a calendar view, selecting room sizes and durations, and receive confirmation emails.
The system should automate fine calculations for overdue items, provide students with a breakdown of fines, and send notifications about overdue items and fines.
Students with outstanding fines should be blocked from new loans or room bookings above a certain threshold, while librarians can manually override fines if needed.
Librarians should have tools for managing inventory and generating reports on loan volumes, popular items, fine revenue, and room utilization metrics.
System must comply with GDPR for handling student data.
The system must provide a user-friendly interface for librarians to manage book inventory, including adding, updating, and retiring items.
The system should provide access to data that highlights loan volumes, popular items, and trends over time for librarians.
The system must prevent double bookings for study rooms.
The booking process for study rooms should be efficient and user-friendly.
Students should receive confirmation emails after making a study room booking.
Students should have the flexibility to book rooms in advance and check availability for same-day bookings.
Students should be able to report returns online, even if returning physical books in person.
Automated email reminders for due dates and fines should be sent to students.
The system should allow students to view their current loans, including due dates and outstanding fines.
Students should have access to clear information regarding how their fines were calculated.
The system should provide librarians with tracking capabilities for room utilization metrics.
